text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-serve-prod queue depth > 10k (5m avg), 40% 429 throttles. Multiple preemption events from spot-pool-usw2 in last 6m. Auto-scaler errors seen. Paging @sre-oncall and @infra-lead.

sre-oncall: Ack. Pulling up dashboards.

eng-runtime: Seeing consistent OOM / worker restarts on pods tied to spot instances. Logs show preemption sigterm then pods stuck in Pending for >3m.

ml-ops: Customer impact? Which customers hit errors?

prod-support: CS queue shows spike for accounts using realtime-embed and chat endpoints; ~12 customers seeing >50% failures. Skipping degraded responses to smaller models.

infra-lead: I see autoscaler failed to create on-demand fallback nodes: aws/compute returned quota error when trying to allocate 8 on-demand GPUs. Investigating.

eng-runtime: Debug logs:
```
2026-03-15T18:12:05Z WARN preemptible-watcher: instance i-0a... terminated by provider (spot reclaim)
2026-03-15T18:12:06Z ERROR autoscaler: launch failed for group spot-pool-usw2: CapacityError: InsufficientInstanceCapacity
2026-03-15T18:12:08Z ERROR autoscaler: fallback-policy="on-demand" start failed: QuotaExceeded
```

sre-oncall: So two simultaneous problems: (1) spot pool being reclaimed, (2) autoscaler can't provision on-demand due to quota/config. Queue backing up because routing still targets spot-only pool.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: routing hotfix job scheduled to fallback to cpu-backend for non-critical embed requests. ID: deploy-9842

eng-runtime: Rolling a quick routing change to divert low-SLO traffic to smaller CPU model and free GPU capacity for high-priority chat. Command: `infractl route update --route /v1/embeddings --policy fallback:cpu --criteria priority!=high`

infra-lead: Doing manual emergency resize for dedicated on-demand group. Running: `cloudctl instances resize --group=ondemand-gpu-usw2 --count=6` — waiting on provider allocation. If that fails, we need quota request now.

ml-ops: Any chance we can change batching to reduce token throughput temporarily? Might help until nodes come up.

eng-runtime: Enabled aggressive batching on live workers (reduction of max-concurrency). Side effect: latency up for some calls, but reduces token burn. Command: `redwoodctl config set --service gpu-serve --batching max_tokens=2048`

prod-support: Noting customer-impacted list and sending templated status update to affected accounts. CS on it.

infra-lead: Provider responded: partial allocation (2/6). Quota request submitted for +10 GPUs, support ticket opened (SR# 992331). ETA unknown.

sre-oncall: Current mitigation status:
- diverts in place for low-priority embeddings (decrease GPU pressure)
- manual on-demand resize + provider ticket in flight
- batching tightened to reduce per-token consumption
- monitoring set to alert at 5k queue

eng-runtime: Traffic snapshot: high-priority chat still seeing elevated p95 latency and some tail 503s as instances come back.

cs-lead: Customers being notified. Critical accounts flagged for personalized outreach.

infra-lead: Manual step worked for control plane: started 2 on-demand nodes now visible. Kube cluster scheduling recovered some pods.

sre-oncall: Observed queue dropping from 10k -> 2.5k over 8 minutes after the staging actions. 429 rate down from 40% -> 12%.

eng-runtime: One wrinkle: autoscaler logs show a race where scale-up requests against spot and on-demand pools were throttled by our internal rate limiter causing retries to fail. I'll file a follow-up to remove the 'single-simultaneous-scale' guard for emergency paths.

infra-lead: For immediate safety, I've toggled routing policy to allow on-demand fallback for all model routes, not just high-priority. Command run: `infractl route set --allow-on-demand true`

prod-support: Error volume subsided but CS still seeing intermittent failures for accounts that use long-run streaming.

ml-ops: Suggest we create an alert rule: if preemptions >3/min AND queue growth >2k in 5m => auto-trigger on-demand allocation and pause non-essential model rollouts.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. Will create ticket and schedule post-incident follow-up.

eng-runtime: Quick notes for postmortem:
- root cause: burst spot preemptions exposed insufficient on-demand fallback (quota + autoscaler race).
- immediate mitigation: routing changes, manual on-demand resize, batching adjustment.
- action items: (1) emergency path for scale-up that bypasses internal rate limiter; (2) permanent increase in on-demand quota or reservation for critical clusters; (3) better preemption simulations in chaos tests.

infra-lead: I've attached SR#992331 link in ticket. Also starting a change to autoscaler to surface quota failures earlier instead of retrying blindly.

deploy-bot: Canary for routing change successful, no regressions detected.

sre-oncall: Handoff to day oncall @eng-runtime for follow-ups. Leaving notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1853456789. Scheduled postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 PT.

eng-runtime: Taking handoff. Will track follow-ups and own the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

cs-lead: Closing CS notification loop after first wave; will update after postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident annotated as HIGH severity. Duration so far: 00:52.

sre-oncall: Marking page resolved. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours and then close if stable.

eng-runtime: Logged action items to ops board and assigned owners.

infra-lead: Final status: queue stable at ~200-300, 429s down to <2%. Closing active mitigation.

prod-support: Thanks all.
